item.title: Badgers make multiple changes to starting lineup after slow start to season
item.description: Austin Rapp #22 of the Wisconsin Badgers dribbles the basketball while being defended by Jordan Rogers #3 of the Denver Pioneers at the Kohl Center in Madison, Wisconsin, on November 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers have not enjoyed the best start to the 2026-27 season, losing both of their games at the Baha Mar Championship last weekend. It has been an underwhelming start for several players for Wisconsin, as they try to figure out their new-look roster that features several transfers and a key freshman contributor. So far, head coach Greg Gard has been tinkering with his rotation minutes, trying to figure out his best lineups, as Wisconsin has seen ups and downs in nearly every game so far this season. To make matters worse, Jack Janicki, a key cog for the Badgers bench, is now out for the season with a foot injury. Well, Gard’s experimenting is now transitioning to the starting lineup, as the Badgers are going with a new starting five against the Northeastern Huskies on Wednesday night. Wisconsin is replacing transfer Eian Elmer with freshman Jackson Ball in the backcourt alongside Owen Foxwell and Braeden Carrington. Additionally, Austin Rapp will make his first start of the year, replacing Victory Onuetu in the starting lineup. Elmer was the Badgers’ prized transfer addition from Miami of Ohio in the offseason. He seemed to be a quality fit on paper with his shooting ability and athleticism on the wing. Elmer had also been testing the NBA Draft waters, receiving some interest there before withdrawing and entering the transfer portal. However, the senior has struggled as of late, and his minutes have diminished as a result. After scoring 18, 11, and 12 points in Wisconsin’s first three games, Elmer was scoreless against Seton Hall last week and had just two points against Murray State. A key issue has been the lack of aggressiveness. Elmer had just one shot attempt against Seton Hall and was 1 for 5 against Murray State. Even in the earlier games, there seemed to be some passiveness from the senior in attacking lanes and initiating offense, and his minutes dwindled as a result. Looking for a spark, Wisconsin is going to the freshman Jackson Ball instead. While he’s seen his ups and downs, Ball has looked to be aggressive when in the game, and had 12 points in his most extended action against Murray State last Friday. In the frontcourt, Austin Rapp is back in the starting lineup for the first time, replacing a struggling Victory Onuetu, who has not looked great to start the year. Rapp had been recovering from an offseason procedure, and the move seemed inevitable, although Wisconsin had also seemed to have an interest in playing Nolan Winter with a center. We’ll see how the Badgers rotation changes as a result, but Wisconsin is going with a new starting five against Northeastern here on Wednesday.

To corroborate this, we were all waiting to go into the locker room after practice. We were watching Rodgers on @PatMcAfeeShow on a TV in the lobby. A team staffer came through and changed the channel to “How I Met Your Mother.” So we all just started watching McAfee on our phones instead. 30 media members. Watching Rodgers shred McCarthy. A few minutes into Rodgers’ diatribe, McCarthy comes walking through all of us to head upstairs after practice. Everyone listening to multiple phones on full volume. I was here for AB’s helicopter. I was here for the Anthem-debacle presser. Tomlin’s presser wandering onto the field in Baltimore. The players ripping Harrison after he went to New England. I’ve covered the Steelers for 25 years. I’ve never seen anything like this before. — Tim Benz (@TimBenzPGH) November 25, 2026 And while Ted Mosby may have needed nine seasons to finish his story, nobody in that lobby was willing to let a sitcom rerun cost them a minute of what Rodgers was saying. The reporters pulled up the broadcast on their own phones instead, and before long several of them were blaring Rodgers’ interview at full volume across the lobby. Roughly 10 minutes after practice wrapped, with Rodgers still in the thick of his monologue, Mike McCarthy emerged and strode straight through the middle of that cacophony on his way upstairs, per ESPN’s Brooke Pryor . PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh , who ranked the moment among the strangest sights of his reporting career, noted that McCarthy looked visibly displeased as he passed through. He had good reason, because the voice filling the lobby — and permeating the locker room — belonged to a quarterback he had benched less than 24 hours earlier. Late Tuesday night, only hours after McCarthy had publicly stood by Rodgers following a listless offensive showing against the Philadelphia Eagles , the Steelers announced that their quarterback would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos and that Mason Rudolph would start in his place. Rodgers told McAfee that word of the benching reached him through tight end Pat Freiermuth rather than his head coach, and that slight became the starting point for an extraordinary account of his relationship with the man who coached him for 13 seasons in Green Bay. By Rodgers’ telling, McCarthy had been dozing off and snoring through meetings and skipping walk-throughs, and he insisted the coach had brought those habits with him from Green Bay. He said he had confronted McCarthy about them for months as a concerned friend. As the Steelers’ offense floundered, Rodgers said those talks shifted to the play calling, which he wanted McCarthy to hand over to someone else, and he eventually spelled out what he expected to happen if the coach wouldn’t. “If you try and bench me or don’t change the play calling, then you should just release me.” A year ago, Rodgers wasn’t appearing on McAfee’s show at all, as the weekly segments that reliably manufactured headlines throughout his years in Green Bay and New York went dark during his first season in Pittsburgh , apparently in deference to Mike Tomlin. Tomlin’s departure instantly revived the question of whether those appearances would return under McCarthy , and Rodgers answered before he had even committed to another season, returning to McAfee’s show in the spring as a pending free agent to discuss his undecided future and his new head coach. Once he signed on for a 22nd season and reported to training camp, the familiar spectacle returned in full. By the time McAfee broadcast live from Latrobe this summer, the quarterback felt emboldened enough to devote his airtime to a broadside against Anthony Fauci , and McCarthy, asked about the episode the following day , showed little appetite for the furor his quarterback had stirred up. “But at the end of the day, my job is to keep it about football, keep the focus on winning,” McCarthy said at the time. That aspiration proved far easier to articulate than to enforce once the games began. Following a Week 3 loss to the New England Patriots, Rodgers accepted responsibility for the sputtering offense at the postgame podium before pivoting to his coach and insinuating that McCarthy needed a keener understanding of what was working so the Steelers could call better plays. Mike Florio saw through the veneer of accountability and condemned it as open disrespect of McCarthy , likening the remarks to Rodgers’ grievances about lethargic sideline energy during their final seasons together in Green Bay and grouping them with his McAfee and Cam Heyward podcast appearances as part of a persistent campaign of passive-aggressive jabs. As it turns out, Rodgers brought back the same concerns about McCarthy’s engagement that he once raised about the energy on Green Bay’s sideline, this time in an airing of grievances that will almost certainly end his NFL career. Rodgers has long insisted he has no interest in television , and the networks reportedly have little interest in him , so there’s no obvious second act waiting for him in the media either. That leaves McAfee’s show as one of the few places still willing to let Rodgers tell his side of the story, and after Wednesday, it might be the only one. Manuel will remain with Michigan until the school finds a full-time replacement, per multiple reports. item.description: Following a hard fall last Friday night at Lucas Oil Stadium during Kentucky’s game against Indiana, star center Malachi Moreno is not expected to play Friday night against Wichita State. Moreno did return to the game against Indiana after briefly leaving in the second half, finishing with 12 points and a team-high seven rebounds in 32 minutes. He also was 6/9 from the field and had two blocks. Mark Pope said on Wednesday that he doesn’t expect Moreno to be able to play Friday, with a UK spokesperson saying Moreno is still in the concussion protocol and is progressing but hasn’t resumed practicing. Moreno is currently third on the team in scoring at 13.8 points per game, and he leads the team with 8.7 rebounds per game and 11 blocks. He’s also shooting an efficient 66.7 percent from the floor and playing 27.8 minutes per game. With Moreno not expected to play Friday, the onus is now on Franck Kepnang and Reece Potter to step in and both fill the void. Kentucky-Wichita State will tip off at 9:00 ET on ESPN2 and the UK Sports Network.

item.description: Red Sox Should Only Sign 12-Year Veteran Under One Condition originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The one question the Red Sox have to consider with their rotation this year is whether they want to bring in another left-handed starter. With Payton Tolle, Garrett Crochet, and Ranger Suarez already in the rotation, adding another left-hander might not be the best decision. The Red Sox, however, might not view that as a big issue, considering those three guys are among the best in baseball. One could already argue that Crochet is a top-five pitcher in the game; Suarez has been lights-out for a very long time and Tolle looks to be a potential star in the making. If Boston is content with bringing in another left-hander, it will make some easier decisions during the offseason. When recently looking at some players who could be fits, the Red Sox's beat reporter for The Athletic recently suggested another left-hander in Matthew Boyd, the Chicago Cubs free agent who posted a 3.91 ERA last season. “Boyd, a veteran lefty, posted a 3.91 ERA in 22 starts over 126 ⅔ innings for the Chicago Cubs last year while also missing time for a meniscus tear. Over two seasons with the Cubs, he posted a 3.50 ERA, 20.2 percent strikeout rate, 6.5 percent walk rate and 39.7 percent groundball rate. Boyd battled injuries for much of 2021-24, but would still be an intriguing option at the back of Boston’s rotation even as another lefty. MLB Trade Rumors projects a one-year, $13 million deal for Boyd,” Jen McCaffrey of The Athletic wrote. In a perfect world, the Red Sox would bring in a right-hander who can get outs at a high level, even if that's similar to Boyd. At the same time, if Boyd can be had for a somewhat low price and the Red Sox feel fine with how their rotation looks, there are far worse options out there. He's been above average for quite some time now and should be more than fine in a Red Sox rotation that has a chance to be very good if everything goes as planned. item.title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy held out of practice for ankle injury suffered in Mexico City game
item.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy talks to Jerry Rice before the game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. (Fernando Llano/Associated Press) It doesn't sound like a serious ailment, but it qualifies as a big deal because it involves the health of the San Francisco 49ers ' franchise quarterback: Brock Purdy didn't practice Wednesday because of an ankle injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan termed Purdy "day-to-day" after he was injured during the second quarter of the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings last Sunday in Mexico City. Shanahan said Purdy didn't have a high ankle sprain, which typically sidelines players for multiple weeks, and that Purdy's injury didn't impact Shanahan's play-calling after he was checked on the sideline. "They always tell you when someone has (an injury), but then they come back and they're like, ‘Hey, checked out. He should be fine,'" Shanahan said. "He didn't miss any plays." Purdy appeared to be injured with 11 seconds left in the second quarter when defensive tackle Jalen Redmond rolled up on his left ankle while pressuring Purdy on a play in which Purdy was flagged for intentional grounding. Before Purdy was injured, with the 49ers leading 28-10, he completed 12 of 15 passes for 176 yards and three touchdown passes. He then completed 9 of 11 passes for 79 yards. Purdy didn't have a rushing attempt. Shanahan downplayed the seriousness of Purdy's injury, but he declined to definitely say he would start against the Seahawks on Sunday at Levi's Stadium. "I mean, he can't (practice) today, so it's always a possibility," Shanahan said. "… It's day-to-day with it, but we've got to see how it goes." If Purdy is unavailable Sunday, the 49ers would turn to Mac Jones , who has thrown one pass while playing 20 mop-up snaps this season. In 2025, Jones went 5-3 as a fill-in starter when Purdy was sidelined with turf toe and ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage (69.6%). This set up a whirlwind effort to find Parker a replacement opponent, resulting in a deal with Martin Bakole. Bakole took the fight on two days’ notice and hopped on an Ethiopian Airlines flight the day before from his native Congo, barely making it to Riyadh at 2 a.m. on the day of the fight. The move turned Bakole into an instant boxing folk hero. Parker didn’t hesitate to say yes to the replacement opponent despite Bakole’s impressive performance in August against Jared Anderson. Credit to Bakole for seizing the opportunity. But he was admittedly not in the greatest shape. Parker defanged several big punchers in his career, including Derek Chisora, Andy Ruiz Jr., Zhilei Zhang, and Deontay Wilder. Bakole became another, as Parker scored a second-round knockout win. Joseph Parker Stumbles Parker was riding high, and next he took on Fabio Wardley. Things didn’t go as well for Parker, who lost by an 11th-round TKO to Wardley in October 2025. Following the loss, Parker received a three-month suspension after testing positive for a cocaine metabolite. Parker denied knowingly using the drug. UK Anti-Doping (UKAD) accepted his claim that the substance entered his system out-of-competition via food contaminated by his nutritionist. item.title: Xavier Musketeers hold off Texas A&M for big Bahamas win
item.description: NASSAU, Bahamas - After a promising start to the season gave way to a frustrating two-game homestand that included an 18-point loss to Iowa, Xavier arrived in the Bahamas with questions to answer and an opportunity to change the conversation surrounding their season. In need of a response, Xavier found one on Wednesday, Nov. 25 by knocking off undefeated Texas A&M , 88-83, in the opening round of the Signature Series of the Battle 4 Atlantis at Imperial Arena. The Musketeers got a much-needed bounce-back victory, and an early-season resume boost against a team that was one spot away from being ranked in the latest AP Top 25 poll. More: Xavier vs. Texas A&M start delayed for roof leak in Bahamas More: Bold predictions for Xavier vs. Texas A&M at Battle 4 Atlantis The victory was especially important for a Xavier team that had seen some of its early momentum disappear during a difficult week at home. The Musketeers needed to scratch and claw for a 75-67 victory over Cleveland State before Iowa took the wind out of Xavier’s sails on its home floor. With Richard Pitino saying Xavier needed to do some “soul-searching,” his team found it in paradise with a decisive performance against a Texas A&M squad that entered the event averaging nearly 100 points per game. Xavier trailed for less than 90 seconds overall and led by as many as 18 in the second half before Texas A&M came storming back to tie it in the final minute of regulation. Despite another tough night at the charity stripe, Xavier hit five free throws in the final 35 seconds and did enough on the defensive end to get a marquee non-conference win. Xavier got a 20-point, 10-rebound double-double from Mike Nwoko, who hit the go-ahead free throws with 35 seconds left. Xavier shot 47.5% overall and had Tru Washington (15) and Gabriel Pozzato (14) in double figures, as well. In his first collegiate start, freshman Kalek House had nine points, four assists and three rebounds. The Musketeers (6-1) now turn their attention to another major opportunity on Friday, Nov. 27, when they face No. 2 Virginia at 11 a.m. A victory over the Cavaliers could potentially transform the outlook of Xavier’s season in a matter of days with back-to-back wins that will hold weight all the way to March. item.title: Wisconsin Badgers vs. Northeastern Huskies Game Thread: Get Right Game?
item.description: PORTLAND, OREGON - MARCH 19: Head coach Greg Gard of the Wisconsin Badgers watches while playing the High Point Panthers during the second half in the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Moda Center on March 19, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. The Panthers won 83-82 in regulation. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a disappointing week at the Baha Mar Championship, the Wisconsin Badgers are facing off against the Northeastern Huskies back at the Kohl Center, with tip-off set for 6:00 p.m. on Big Ten Network. Wisconsin’s season took another rough turn last week, as they lost 74-69 to Seton Hall before getting blown out 70-53 to Murray State in the third-place game. In both games, the Badgers saw huge deficits in the first half that they weren’t able to overcome. To make matters worse, Wisconsin lost senior reserve guard Jack Janicki for the season due to a foot injury in the Murray State game. Now, head coach Greg Gard will need to figure out his rotation, which he’s tinkered with a bit already in the first six games of the season. Now, Wisconsin takes on Northeastern on Wednesday evening, and they’re 20.5-point favorites heading into the game. The Badgers have now been 20+ point favorites in five of their seven games so far, but have covered in only one of the first four, with all of their other wins coming by single digits. Northeastern has started the year 2-4 with losses to Boston, Virginia, Butler, and Stonehill. They’ve allowed 90+ points in three games, while also giving up 84 points to Butler. This feels like a potential get-right game for the Badgers, but they’ve also underwhelmed against opponents they’ve been heavily favored over so far this season. Can Wisconsin rebound with a strong performance on Wednesday? Join us as our game thread is officially open!

item.title: Report: Kevin Gausman Agrees to One-Year Deal with Tigers
item.description: Sep 30, 2026; San Diego, California, USA; Chicago Cubs pitcher Kevin Gausman (12) delivers a pitch in the first inning against the San Diego Padres during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Mandatory … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Right-handed starting pitcher Kevin Gausman has agreed to a one-year contract with the Detroit Tigers, according to ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The contract is worth $25 million for the 2027 season. Aug 18, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Cubs pitcher Kevin Gausman (12) pitches against the Chicago White Sox during the first inning at Wrigley Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Kevin Gausman’s 2026 Season Gausman, 35, split last season between the Toronto Blue Jays and Chicago Cubs. In 32 starts between the two teams, Gausman went 9-12 with a 4.51 ERA. The Cubs acquired the Colorado native at the trade deadline to bolster their rotation. He was serviceable down the stretch, posting a 4-2 record with a 4.83 ERA. Right-hander Kevin Gausman and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $25 million contract, pending physical, sources tell ESPN. Gausman, 35, is one of the best workhorses in baseball, with the second-most innings of any pitcher since 2021. — Jeff Passan (@JeffPassan) November 25, 2026 Gausman’s Career So Far This will be Gausman’s 15th year in the major leagues. He is joining his seventh team. His longest tenure with an organization was with the Baltimore Orioles, where he pitched from 2013-2018. He has also played for the Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds , San Francisco Giants , Blue Jays, and Cubs. He has had multiple standout seasons. His first came in 2021, when he won 14 games and helped the Giants win 107 games (a franchise record) and the National League West Division title. He finished sixth in Cy Young voting that season. With the Blue Jays, Gausman finished third in Cy Young voting in 2023 and posted 14 wins in 2024. In 2025, he helped the Blue Jays reach the World Series by posting a 2.93 ERA in six appearances. The Last Word The Tigers are getting a pitcher who is the definition of reliable. Kevin Gausman may not be an ace at this point, but he can be an effective middle-of-the-rotation starter. The Tigers can count on 30+ starts from Gausman. Perhaps Gausman’s most valuable asset is his ability to work deep into games. In a league where managers are not hesitant to go to their bullpen, Gausman can provide a cushion for the Tigers’ bullpen. This is a solid addition for the Tigers. Kevin Gausman won’t move the needle as an ace, but he adds needed durability to the rotation. This is a smart investment for a team looking to return to October and make some noise. Now another sport with a paddle is becoming part of the game plan as we move into 2027 . The hottest amenity drawing attention is padel, a fast-growing racquet activity that blends elements of tennis, squash and other sports and has become one of the newest status symbols at private clubs around the country. Padel is pronounced "pah-DEL" rather than like the word "paddle." For sure, the Sunshine State's country clubs are no longer competing solely on golf courses, clubhouses and dining rooms as part of their business models. And padel, which originated in Mexico in 1969 and slowly started as a niche in Spain and Argentina, is now bouncing into the formula. Here's what to know about padelistas invading Southwest Florida. Where did padel show up this month in Naples, Florida for the first time? At Quail Creek Country Club in North Naples this month, members officially opened their glass-walled three-court padel complex and touted the activity's introduction to Southwest Florida private clubs. They see it as part of a larger shift in how residents and others want to spend their time while saying it puts Quail Creek on the forefront of the global social-sport movement, bringing the activity to Naples and the region. Now another sport with a paddle is becoming part of the game plan as we move into 2027 . The hottest amenity drawing attention is padel, a fast-growing racquet activity that blends elements of tennis, squash and other sports and has become one of the newest status symbols at private clubs around the country. Padel is pronounced "pah-DEL" rather than like the word "paddle." For sure, the Sunshine State's country clubs are no longer competing solely on golf courses, clubhouses and dining rooms as part of their business models. And padel, which originated in Mexico in 1969 and slowly started as a niche in Spain and Argentina, is now bouncing into the formula. Here's what to know about padelistas invading Southwest Florida. Where did padel show up this month in Naples, Florida for the first time? At Quail Creek Country Club in North Naples this month, members officially opened their glass-walled three-court padel complex and touted the activity's introduction to Southwest Florida private clubs. They see it as part of a larger shift in how residents and others want to spend their time while saying it puts Quail Creek on the forefront of the global social-sport movement, bringing the activity to Naples and the region. "We're fostering a thriving community around this kinetic sport," Quail Creek General Manager Chris Evans said. “We couldn’t have accomplished this without the vision and leadership of our director of court sports, Jose Pastrello. He has been a champion of the sport, the project, our club and of Naples." Besides padel, what other offerings are included at the Quail Creek CC? It joins tennis, pickleball and bocce as part of an expanding menu of recreational offerings designed to appeal to multiple generations of residents in the Valewood Drive community. So how did it happen at Quail Creek? Where did the inspiration to get padel to Naples, Florida? Was it Miami? Pastrello is president of the Florida Division of the Racquet Sports Professionals Association known as RSPA, which has been discussing the sport. “I was first inspired to bring padel to Naples through our RSPA meetings," Pastrello said. "I was hearing how successful it’s been at other clubs, and after a visit with some Quail Creek members to a club in Miami, I knew right away that our member community would embrace the challenge and social quality of padel." 'Padel has the energy of pickleball, and the technical aspects of tennis' It's the right match for the community, Pastrello said. “Padel has the energy of pickleball, and the technical aspects of tennis, while still being easy to learn,” he said. "I am beyond thrilled to introduce it here. I have so much energy for the sport." What is padel and when and where was it first introduced in the U.S.? Played on an enclosed court roughly two-thirds the size of a traditional tennis court, the sport combines elements of tennis, squash, racquetball and, to some observers, pickleball. Players use solid perforated rackets and can play the ball off the surrounding glass and mesh walls, creating longer rallies and a highly social atmosphere, according to the International Padel Federation, known as FIP. It was first introduced in the U.S. in 1993 by Argentine native Felipe Arnold and his business partner Ed Thompson at the Houstonian Hotel Club and Spa, according to USA Padel, the national governing body recognized by FIP. More: New $350 million waterfront community coming to East Naples How many play padel in the United States? What major event this week? The annual report from USA Padel shows its membership has blown up from 500 in 2022 to nearly 3,000 in 2025. In that time, its number of U.S. clubs has grown from 30 to more than 100. But the actual American number of Padel participants just exceeded more than a million for the first time, according to Sports & Fitness Industry Association's 2026 sport involvement study. About a quarter of them played at least eight times in a year's time. USA Padel's national team of 56 male and female players ages 35 and more are in Paraguay right now for the Senior Pan American Championship 2026. Last week, its U.S. National Women’s Absolute Team finished 11th place at the FIP World Cup 2026 in Qatar, a four-spot leap from its 15th-place two years ago. Earlier this month, the men landed 13th as they did in 2024. How many play the sport of padel worldwide, and in how many countries? FIP says the sport now has more than 40 million players worldwide and is played in more than 190 countries and territories. The organization reported court construction worldwide has continued to grow at double-digit rates annually. That has received the attention of Florida country clubs like Quail Creek looking to widen their scope beyond golf by adding pickleball, wellness centers, social clubs and new dining venues in an effort to attract younger members, create activities that appeal to entire families and provide year-round engagement for residents and seasonal members. What new connection did padel have to the PGA in 2026 in Florida? The latest trend was visible at this year's PGA Show in Orlando, where padel shared floor space for the first time ever with traditional golf equipment and technology. The sport's rapid growth has become especially noticeable in Florida, where private clubs and developers are racing to add courts. Palm Beach County, for one, has a head start on Southwest Florida, which, for example, has a Smash Point racquet site planning a debut next year on Park Meadows Drive in Fort Myers and has a random court here and there, like a local academy that offers it but primarily markets itself for tennis. How is Palm Beach ahead of Southwest Florida on the sport of padel? Famed The Breakers tennis center expanded last year to include padel. Boca Raton was opening Wednesday what its developers say is Florida's largest indoor pickleball and padel compound , 100,000 square feet of luxury, with each court equipped with cameras and 70-inch monitors allowing players to track scores, replay points and share their plays with coaches and social media. And a new private club on a March completion track with six padel courts, six tennis courts and at least two or so pickleball courts has a waiting list of 700 applicants beyond the 100 original members. Situating it on Billionaire's Row, casino and resort mogul Steve Wynn got the first approval for one in the town of Palm Beach. But it's not been smooth for all padel plutocrats. Palm Beach and neighbors pushed back last month against plans by billionaire Nelson Peltz and his wife to stick a padel court atop a basketball court on his 13-acre oceanfront estate. Earlier this year, the Peltzes — the in-laws of soccer player David Beckham and former Spice Girl Victoria Beckham — ended up having to rip out a previous one they had installed after it sparked a code-violation case . What international soccer superstar is retiring so he can 'play padel?' However, padel's popularity has another soccer superstar contemplating retirement. Cristiano Ronaldo recently revealed plans to potentially retire next year, partly so he can “watch and play padel, which I really like.” And earlier this month, tennis star John McEnroe and golfer Matt Kucher, who also is big into ping pong, played each other in Mexico . As the Celtics have struggled recently, despite still sitting in second place in the Eastern Conference, it's raised questions about what the front office might do before the NBA trade deadline. The Celtics already made one of the biggest moves of the past decade by sending Jaylen Brown to the 76ers in a deal involving Paul George, but as Brad Stevens has shown in the past, when he thinks he has to push buttons, he'll do just that. The Celtics will have an opportunity to improve before the deadline, but as always, it'll come down to what it could cost. According to the latest, despite questions about moving on from players like Derrick White or Sam Hauser, there's no plan to do so, and it would be considered a "shock" if it happened. “Remember, the Celtics came into this season with a focus on staying below the luxury tax and making their move in the offseason. “The losing streak has been unsightly, but it is not going to change the organization from that goal. It would be a shock if players like Derrick White or even Sam Hauser hit the market,” Sean Deveney of Heavy reported . White is a very good player in his own right, but he has slowed down a bit after really impressing in those first couple of years in Boston. The past year or so hasn't been too kind to him as he's taken on a bigger offensive role. This season, perhaps uglier than any other that he's played in Boston, has frankly been inexcusable. It's certainly part of the reason why the Celtics have lost recently, as he's made just three 3-pointers in the last three games on 25 attempts prior to the win against Washington. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy during a game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went off on head coach Mike McCarthy during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Rodgers revealed that McCarthy falls asleep during meetings and snores, and just flat-out misses meetings, too. He thinks McCarthy is unhealthy and his mind is not in the right place. He explained that McCarthy said “1–2-3 Packers” at halftime of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. “We were like what the f*** is going on?” Rodgers said of his teammate’s reactions. “Eight years removed [from Green Bay] and this is a game we need to win.” Rodgers said he genuinely is concerned about McCarthy. “I’m not telling you this to f***ing bury you, but this isn’t healthy and becoming of someone calling the plays,” Rodgers told his longtime head coach. On Wednesday, McCarthy did not comment on the sleeping in meetings part, but he did admit that he said “1–2-3 Packers” at halftime of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. McCarthy called Rodgers’ 1-2-3 Packers story “embarrassing” and an honest mistake. “The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional. There were conversations prior to that. It was an embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments,” McCarthy said. McCarthy also said he just had a meeting with the team’s leadership council, and believes he has the support of the locker room. “It was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind. … I’m proud of our leadership,” McCarthy said. The Steelers organization is also offering McCarthy “full support” and has no “immediate” plans to fire him, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. “Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, the subject of Aaron Rodgers accusations today, has the full support of the organization, sources say. They are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes,” Rapoport wrote. The Steelers revealed late Tuesday night that they’ve benched Rodgers and that he would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. They are also in the process of releasing the four-time NFL MVP. “There was an ultimatum made that was clearly out of his job description, so I made the decision to bench him,” McCarthy said on Wednesday. Rodgers said it was contentious during his last conversation with McCarthy. Rodgers told McCarthy that he thought it was in the best interest of the team for somebody else to call plays and if not, they should release him. item.title: What Happened to Davante Adams, and When Will He Return? Latest on Rams WR’s Injury and Why He’s Out in Week 12 vs. Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
item.description: What Happened to Davante Adams, and When Will He Return? Latest on Rams WR’s Injury and Why He’s Out in Week 12 vs. Packers on Thanksgiving Eve Davante Adams isn’t playing in the Los Angeles Rams’ Thanksgiving Eve game against his former team, the Green Bay Packers, on Wednesday night. Asked Friday about a Week 12 return for Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson, head coach Sean McVay admitted: “We’re not quite there yet.” McVay did say there is “a possibility” that Adams plays the following game in Week 13 against the Kansas City Chiefs on Dec. 3. On Monday, two days before kickoff at SoFi Stadium, he backed the receivers who will play in place of Adams and Puka Nacua, whose season is over after surgery. Sean McVay Vouches for the Receivers Filling in for Davante Adams McVay was asked on Monday whether passing on a receiver at the trade deadline was the right decision. “Based on last week, I’m excited about what those guys that did get opportunities did,” he said. “Let’s continue to see if we can grow and figure out what it looks like. You know the information that I had at the time, but I don’t want it to ever be misunderstood. I am confident in Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith and C.J. item.title: Patriots Insider Reveals Why Team Doesn't Want Daniel Jones
item.description: Patriots Insider Reveals Why Team Doesn't Want Daniel Jones originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Patriots ' season hangs by a thread, many have started to believe the team could find a proven quarterback to save it as Drake Maye continues to recover from his injury. With Daniel Jones available, as the Indianapolis Colts released him and he cleared waivers, he was instantly viewed as a potential option in New England. However, head coach Mike Vrabel made it clear Monday morning that he has no plans to bring in another quarterback. That may change depending on how things go for Tommy DeVito and the Patriots' offense against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday afternoon in Los Angeles. However, the latest reasoning for Jones not being on the Patriots' radar makes some sense. While he's undoubtedly a better player than DeVito at this stage of his career, a Patriots beat reporter for The Athletic suggested that New England doesn't want to bring in Jones to learn this offense and hope everything will go as planned. “For starters, even if Jones is probably slightly better than DeVito, the team doesn’t seem to feel like the gap between them is so wide that it’s worth putting Jones through a crash course on an offense DeVito already understands well. The coaching staff has worked with DeVito for a year. The staff appreciates his work ethic and has been impressed by some throws in preseason games. “Now, the Patriots want to roll with the backup-level quarterback they know — and, crucially, the one who knows their system — over the one they don’t,” Chad Graff of The Athletic wrote . Because DeVito already understands this offense, it's not wrong to think that Vrabel and the Patriots are making the right decision here. The problem with DeVito is that he hasn't really proven much throughout his career, playing in just 15 games and throwing for nine touchdowns and four interceptions. He had a nice little run with the New York Giants in 2023, but he hasn't done much since. In a way, the same can be said about Jones, but he has much more experience and has, frankly, proven more at this point. item.title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
item.description: Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s. “I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either. Continue reading...

item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
